l.i: non pauca sunt flumina, quæ cum longo interuallo
apparent, tandem alicubi se abscondant in terræ ui-
sceribus, & non multo post iterum emerguntiut [?] Lycus
amnis in Asia, Erasinus in Argolica, Tygris in
Mesopotamia.

main_text.l: Quas ob causas tum aquæ, tum terræ,

l.i: Compertum est, quibus locis nunc mare est uel aliæ
aquæ, ijsdem fuisse olim uastam terram: & uice uersa, ubi
nunc terra est, ibi quondam fuisse aquas. Sic an-
tiquitus tota Ægyptus urbe, quam Thebas uocant,
constabat, teste etiam Homero: nunc uero latissimè
patet, multis undiq; terris circumpositis, &c.
Itaq; huius mutationis causæ dignæ sunt inquisitione.
animalia à cœlo præcipuè accipiunt suæ conditionis &
alterationis modum, ut primùm quidè quasi in iu-
uenta floreát, deinde robur ac magnitudinè tanquàm
uirilem ætatem induant, tandem uero quasi senio
languescát atq; extinguantur: ita terra & aqua ca-
lore atq; frigore à Solis siderumq; motu proueniên
tibus uariè afficiuntur, ac terra quidem modò quasi
in uirenti ætate humore undique perfunditur,
modò uero quasi senio confecta arescit & siccatur:
aquæ autem aliquando uno loco cedūt, moxq; alium
locum nouum occupant.

page.notes: The printed page number is small and partly unclear; read as 323 (possibly 325). The marginal note reads "Lib.I." with "cap.14" beneath it. The word "emerguntiut" is printed as shown and is doubtful. The signature "x 2" at the foot is partly faint. The question paragraph is set in larger roman type, so it is treated as a level 2 heading. The paragraph "1. Causa formalis" is a numbered paragraph, not a heading.
